title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The base is S_0 (eventually S = Spec Ẑ). M is a rank-2 lattice (constant group scheme) with basis λ0, λ1. S_3 acts on it by ρλ0 = λ1 and ρλ1 = −λ0−λ1, with σ swapping λ0 and λ1. Equivalently, M = (Zλ0+Zλ1+Zλ2)/(λ0+λ1+λ2), with S_3 permuting three generators. This looks like the abelianized fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, with loops λ0, λ1, λ∞ around the three punctures, but that reading is my inference. There is an extension E of S_3 by M with fixed lifts ρ, σ satisfying ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1 and σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}λ1. A 'scaling' of (243) is a new pair of lifts ρ' = ξρ, σ' = ησ (ξ, η sections of M) satisfying the S_3 relations. In other words it is a splitting of the extension, i.e. a homomorphic section S_3 → E.

Previous page:
- ρ'^3 = 1 is automatic because 1+ρ+ρ^2 = 0 on M.
- σ'^2 = 1 means (1+σ)η = 0, i.e. η = bδ with δ = λ1−λ0.
- Writing ξ = a0λ0 + a1λ1, the relation σ'ρ'σ'^{-1} = ρ'^{-1} becomes, after left multiplication by ρ: ρ(σ(ξ))·λ1 = ρ(η)^{-1} ξ^{-1} η.

This page:
- Additively, with ε1 = ρσ: ε1(ξ) + λ1 = −ρ(η) − ξ + η, i.e. (1+ε1)(ξ) + λ1 = (1−ρ)(η) (eq. 249).
- Explicitly, ε1 fixes λ1 and sends λ0 to −λ0−λ1. Hence (1+ε1)(ξ) = (2a1−a0)λ1, and (1−ρ)(bδ) = 3bλ1.
- The condition is therefore 2a1 − a0 + 1 = 3b (eq. 250).
- For given ξ, a compatible η exists iff 2a1 − a0 + 1 ≡ 0 mod 3 (eq. 251). It is then unique provided 3 is a non-zero-divisor on the coefficients (true over Ẑ).
- So the scalings form a scheme Sc ≅ {(a0,a1,b) : 2a1−a0−3b = −1} (eq. 252). This is a principal homogeneous space (torsor) under the lattice K = ker(Z^3 → Z, (α0,α1,β) ↦ 2α1−α0−3β) ≅ Z^2, which is the group of crossed homomorphisms Z^1(S_3, M).

Next page: M acts on Sc by conjugation, through the map M → K, c0λ0+c1λ1 ↦ (c0+c1, 2c1−c0, c1−c0). In the coordinates (α1, β) of K this map has determinant 1, so it is an isomorphism. Hence H^1(S_3, M) = 0: all scalings are M-conjugate. The point of the whole computation is to classify and parametrize the S_3-splittings (presumably 'tangential/rigidification' data) in an abelianized fundamental-group extension, within the Longue Marche study of Galois action on fundamental groups of P^1−{0,1,∞} and moduli.
errors: The first line, as machine-transcribed, reads '= ρ_M(η) − ξ + η'. From the previous page's equation ρ(σξ)·λ1 = ρ(η)^{-1}ξ^{-1}η, the correct additive form is '= −ρ_M(η) − ξ + η'. Only with the minus sign does (249), with (1−ρ_M)(η), follow. The sign is probably present in the manuscript and dropped in transcription.

The uniqueness claim correctly requires that 3 be a non-zero-divisor (and, for existence, the congruence mod 3). Over a general base, existence would require divisibility by 3 in Γ(G_0), not merely a congruence. Grothendieck's hypothesis on S covers the case S = Spec Ẑ. Otherwise the computations check out: 1+ε1 = (2a1−a0)λ1 and (1−ρ)δ = 3λ1.

ideas.what: Lifts of S_3 generators in an extension 1→M→E→S_3→1 ('scalings') parametrized by solutions of a linear equation; the set of splittings is a torsor under crossed homomorphisms Z^1(S_3,M)
ideas.modern_name: Splittings of a group extension as a torsor under Z^1(G,M); conjugacy classes = H^1(G,M)
ideas.where_published: Similar torsor/gerbe formalism pervades SGA/Giraud; this specific computation appears unpublished

ideas.what: Explicit S_3-lattice M = Z^3/Z(1,1,1) (A2-type) and the computation that M → Z^1(S_3,M) is an isomorphism, i.e. H^1(S_3,M) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Vanishing of H^1 of S_3 with coefficients in the A2 weight-type lattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; follows from 0→Z→Z^3→M→0 and Shapiro's lemma

ideas.what: Possible interpretation: S_3-symmetry data (rigidifications) in the abelianized fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞} over Spec Ẑ, as part of the Longue Marche program
ideas.modern_name: S_3-equivariance / tangential base points in anabelian geometry of the projective line minus three points
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) circulated; this continuation (pp. 650bis–787) is unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine linear/cohomological computation (splittings of an S_3-extension by a rank-2 lattice, H^1 = 0). The context in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation is of historical interest, but this page contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top likely '701' rather than '70 n'.
First line: '= −ρ_M(η) − ξ + η' (minus sign before ρ_M(η)); the word after it is 'ou encore', not 'on encore'.
'on encore, par un calcul immédiat' should read 'ou encore, par un calcul immédiat'.
'pour qu'il existe η (i.e. ξ')' should read 'η (i.e. σ')'.
'(lire pour ρ' donné)' is probably '(lire pour ξ donné)', an insertion qualifying 'pour ξ ∈ ΓM'.
In (252) the coefficient group written 'E' / 'ℤ√' is probably G_0, resp. ℤδ (η ranges over multiples of δ).
'qui est d. homogène princ. sous Γ' is probably 'qui est principal homogène sous [Sc_0]', i.e. a torsor, continued on the next page.
